registrations.presentation: 955 kcal, Amino acid 40 g, Lipid 50 g, Carbohydrate 80 g Emulsion for Injection for I.V. Infusion
registrations.packaging: Three-Chamber Plastic Bag Made of a Transparent, Colorless Multi-Layer Polymer Film x 1.25 L, 1.875 L and 2.5 L (Bag of 1's & Box of 5's)

summary: Nutriflex Omega Peri (B. Braun Melsungen AG) is a lower-osmolarity three-chamber bag of amino acids with electrolytes, glucose and a lipid emulsion containing medium-chain triglycerides, soybean oil and omega-3-acid triglycerides, for peripheral infusion. Philippine registrations: 1.25, 1.875 and 2.5 L bags. It is a standard formula containing potassium and phosphate.
composition_notes: Source is the Irish SmPC of the same B. Braun product sold in Ireland as Omeflex peri; its 1250 ml column (955 kcal, 40 g amino acids, 50 g lipid, 80 g carbohydrate) matches the Philippine registration exactly. Confirm against the Philippine package insert.
dosing_limits: Adults: maximum daily dose 40 ml/kg body weight; maximum infusion rate 2.0 ml/kg/hour (SmPC 4.2).
kidney_notes: Contraindicated in "severe renal insufficiency in absence of renal replacement therapy" and in disturbances of the electrolyte and fluid balance (SmPC 4.3).
Give with caution to patients with impaired cardiac or renal function; experience in renal failure is limited (SmPC 4.4).
Use caution with drugs that raise serum potassium, such as ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers and potassium-sparing diuretics (SmPC 4.5).

Refeeding may cause hypokalemia, hypophosphatemia and hypomagnesemia; close monitoring of serum electrolytes is required, with checks of water balance, acid-base balance and renal function (SmPC 4.4).
guideline_heading: How it fits the ESPEN 2021 kidney nutrition guideline
guideline: ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 18 (Grade of recommendation 0 – Consensus (82.6% agreement)): protein intakes that may be prescribed are 0.6–0.8 g/kg body weight (BW)/d for a hospitalized patient with CKD without acute/critical illness; 1.2 g/kg BW/d with CKD and KF on conventional intermittent chronic KRT without acute/critical illness; 0.8–1.0 g/kg BW/d with AKI or AKI on CKD without acute/critical illness; start with 1 g/kg BW/day and gradually increase up to 1.3 g/kg BW/d if tolerated with acute/critical illness not on KRT; 1.3–1.5 g/kg/d for critically ill patients on conventional intermittent KRT; and 1.5 g/kg/d up to 1.7 g/kg/d for critically ill patients on continuous KRT (CKRT) or prolonged intermittent KRT (PIKRT). "If available, the pre-hospitalization body weight or usual body weight may be preferred over the ideal BW. Actual BW should not be considered for a protein prescription." (AKI, acute kidney injury.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 25: "The choice of the most appropriate EN or PN formula should be made based on the calorie and protein ratio to provide the most accurate dosing in clinical practice." Grade of recommendation B – Strong consensus (91.3% agreement). (PN, parenteral nutrition.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 24: "No disease-specific enteral nor parenteral formula oriented for patients with reduced kidney function should be routinely utilized in every patient with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF in comparison to conventional formulas. Instead, their use is to be individualized (see recommendation 26)." Grade of recommendation B – Consensus (87.5% agreement).

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 26: "In selected patients with electrolyte and fluid imbalances, concentrated “renal” EN or PN formulas with lower electrolyte content may be preferred over standard formulas." Grade of recommendation GPP – Strong consensus (95.7% agreement). (GPP, good practice point.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 31: "Electrolytes abnormalities are common in patients with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF receiving KRT and shall be closely monitored." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (100% agreement).

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 29: "Serum glucose levels shall be maintained between 140–180 mg/dl in hospitalized patients with AKI, AKI on CKD, or CKD with KF." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (95.5% agreement). Recommendation 30: "Tight glucose control (80–110 mg/dl) shall not be pursued because of the increased risk of hypoglycemia." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (100% agreement).

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 14: "For patients undergoing KRT, the total energy provision by additional calories given in the form of citrate, lactate, and glucose from dialysis/hemofiltration solutions should be included in the calculations to determine the total daily energy provision to avoid overfeeding." Grade of recommendation B – Strong consensus (100% agreement). (KRT, kidney replacement therapy.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 4: "Intradialytic parenteral nutrition (IDPN) shall be applied in malnourished non-critically ill hospitalized patients with CKD and KF on hemodialysis, or the same patients if at risk of malnutrition that fail to respond or do not tolerate ONS or EN." Grade of recommendation A – Strong consensus (91.7% agreement). (CKD, chronic kidney disease; KF, kidney failure; ONS, oral nutritional supplements; EN, enteral nutrition.)

ESPEN 2021 Recommendation 27: "There is not enough evidence to support the routine use of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFA) supplements or PN solutions enriched with omega-3 PUFA in hospitalized patients with AKI, AKI on CKD or CKD with KF." Grade of recommendation GPP – Strong consensus (95.8% agreement).
bottom_line: A standard peripheral bag with an omega-3-containing lipid; ESPEN finds the evidence insufficient to use omega-3-enriched PN routinely in kidney disease. In severe renal insufficiency it needs renal replacement therapy; count its potassium and phosphate, and watch potassium closely with RAAS blockers.
